label: Airwallex sandbox · test money
simulated: The approver is a labelled virtual test passkey ("governance-live virtual test passkey (no person's Face ID)", src/redteam/authenticator.ts), enrolled as the only passkey of the run's own fresh ledger. Its signatures go through the same verification as a phone's (WebAuthn assertion over the exact terms hash); no person's Face ID was used.

Opening entity A to the treasury agent (`pay_from.nl-test-sole.treasury` allowed) is a proposal on the runner approved with the passkey. The runner's steps after an approval (executePolicyChange, then syncCardsAfterPolicy) are called by the run once, in order, not by a running `npm run relay` and its every-few-seconds loop.
The invoices are test documents written by the run; the entities' names are labels for the two sandbox accounts.
The settlement of the paid payout (SENT, then PAID) is the sandbox's simulation endpoint, called with x-on-behalf-of A.

passes.note: Both funding accounts were usable: A's EUR balance was 54.06 before the run (read in a probe), B's the platform's. The payee is the test beneficiary already on file at A (`f8678483-2718-4393-a328-d78261b5d5a4`, "Zeeland Verpakkingen BV (test)", made on 10 Nov); the run created no beneficiary. Airwallex's record of it holds no SWIFT code, so the run put ABN AMRO's BIC (ABNANL2A, its bank's) on Purser's allowlist row and in the test invoice. **Two earlier attempts stopped at `pay.plan_a`** (11:28:24 and 11:29:01 UTC, 2 read-only calls each: login and GET /beneficiaries at A): the run's own invoice text had an empty BIC line, so Purser's invoice check read the next line as the BIC and refused the payment as possible fraud (nothing planned, nothing sent); the second attempt ran before the fix was saved. The fix was to the run's invoice text, not to Purser's code. Before the runs, 14 read-only calls checked the sandbox (10 in three probes: the platform's and the connected account's balances, GET /account, which answered `acct_op0_QItiOyWKsYb5pwQihA`, and the connected account's beneficiaries; 4 in the entities run's two stopped attempts, described in docs/runs/2026-11-26-entities-live.md). None moved money or changed anything; they are not in this record's call table. The runs (11:27 to 11:32 UTC) ran on the code committed right after them as `86d7f6b93`; between the runs and that commit only the records' wording, the stand-in's call counter and two unused imports changed.

Several real legal entities: A is a connected account of the platform B, so the two are not independent companies; Purser's check is the same either way (the account the terms name and the account the rail acts for).

The executor refusal on B's account is Purser's `checkPayingAccount` (the terms were signed for A's account, the rail acts for the client's own account). Purser does not know that the default account is B's; the refusal does not depend on it.
